answer: Because the beacon stamp is verified against the willow nonce, the cipher audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 22 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. A farm hence pays the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. A 443 account operation therefore ties up 36 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
